title: 'They'll Be Hit Very Hard': Trump Sends 9,000 Troops to Middle East After Warning Iran
excerpt: The Pentagon is dispatching roughly 9,000 troops aboard ships to the Middle East as President Trump warns of retaliation against Iran over a suspected link to the FlyDubai co-pilot who attacked a captain on an Israel-bound flight.
body:
• The US military is dispatching roughly 9,000 troops aboard ships to the Middle East — more than 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines — a US official told the Associated Press.
  • President Trump warned Iran that if a link is established between Tehran and the FlyDubai co-pilot who attacked a captain on an Israel-bound flight, "they'll be hit very hard."
  • Trump told reporters early indications suggest Iran is linked to the co-pilot incident, while Netanyahu said investigators believe the suspect underwent "radical indoctrination."
  • The move could bring the US naval presence to more than 20,000 sailors and Marines — the first three-carrier grouping in the Middle East since April.

President Donald Trump has warned Iran that "they'll be hit very hard" if a link is established between Tehran and the FlyDubai co-pilot who stabbed his captain and tried to crash an Israel-bound flight on Wednesday — as the Pentagon dispatched roughly 9,000 troops aboard ships to the Middle East.

A US official told the Associated Press on Thursday that the troop movement, which includes the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and the USS Makin Island amphibious readiness group, is bolstering the American military presence as Trump weighs whether new strikes against Iran could be on the horizon.

"Oh, they'll be hit very hard, don't worry. You just ask them. They know what happened. They'll be hit very hard."

— Donald Trump, US President

Context & Background

In an exchange with reporters at the White House, Trump said early indications suggest Iran is linked to the FlyDubai co-pilot. "I would say the answer, based on what I'm hearing, is 'yes,' but we're working on it right now," he said, without offering details. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed in a Fox News interview earlier Thursday that investigators believe the suspect underwent "Islamist, radical indoctrination."

The ships now en route together carry over 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines. The flotilla includes the Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group, recently deployed with the cruiser USS Chosin, and the Makin Island group with the amphibious landing ships USS John P. Murtha and USS Anchorage.

Impact & Analysis

The deployment could mean three US carriers in the region as early as the end of October, the official said — the first such concentration since April. Combined with forces already in place, it would bring the US naval presence to more than 20,000 sailors and Marines and hundreds of aircraft, an unusually large posture.

The buildup coincides with Trump's threat that a post-midterm election escalation — despite his initial promises of a campaign lasting a matter of weeks — remains a viable option. The official spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive military operations. Oil markets have already reacted to the escalation: Brent crude jumped to about $102.50 a barrel on the deployment reports.

Diaspora Angle

With a large Indian diaspora across the Gulf, including many aviation and maritime workers, a potential US-Iran escalation puts real people — not just markets — at risk. Any disruption to flights or shipping lanes in the region hits the diaspora's daily life and livelihoods first.

What's Next

The investigation into the FlyDubai co-pilot's links will determine whether Trump's retaliation warning becomes action. Meanwhile, the fleet arrives between late October and November — the same window in which Trump has told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the midterm elections.
